concept: A unit of work on the board (GLOSSARY: Task)
note: Counted at seeding: de "Aufgabe" 120 values, de "Task" 1; en "task" 123 values, en "to-do" 5. Known limit: de "Task" also hits "Tasks" (intended) and compounds such as "Taskleiste" (no value today); no unrelated collision at seeding.

concept: Where a task lives: Local, Notion, Todoist (GLOSSARY: Task source)
note: Earlier form: "Verbindung" / "connection". Names where a task lives, Local included: the sources page, the add target, the command palette group. A source that is an integration (Notion, Todoist, Apple Reminders) is also a Verbindung (term integration); Local is a Speicherort, never a Verbindung. A network problem stays "Keine Verbindung" / "No connection", and a source with a problem is "Verbindung prüfen" (term needs-attention). "Datenquelle"/"data source" names the Notion database data source in notion.database.* (the Notion API term): a different concept, not an avoid form. Code identifiers and the {source} placeholder keep their name. Pitfall: a bare "source" in avoidEn would hit every {source} placeholder.

concept: The source new tasks go to unless the user picks another (GLOSSARY: Default source)
note: de "Standard" 7 values, en "Default" 6 values (en also writes "Standard" once).

concept: A task source outside the app: Notion, Todoist (GLOSSARY: Integration)
note: Earlier form: "Integration" / "integration". A task source outside the app, such as Notion or Todoist: de "Verbindung", en "connection". Local is a source (term task-source), not an integration. Notion's own words stay where the text points at Notion's screens (the path "Notion › Einstellungen › Integrationen", "Notion-Integrationstoken") and GitHub's permission names stay as GitHub writes them.

concept: Adding an integration to the board (GLOSSARY: Connect)
note: en "connect" is consistent. de "Verbindung" is the noun for an integration (term integration); where a task lives is a "Speicherort" (term task-source). en "link" (the noun, 5 values for URLs) is not an avoid form: it cannot be told from the verb under word-prefix matching, so "linked" and "link up" stand in for it.

concept: Removing an integration from the board; its tasks stay in the integration (GLOSSARY: Connect / disconnect)
note: Ending an integration connection (user answer: removing an integration = Trennen). de "Trennen" 8 values, en "disconnect" 8. Data removal is delete, taking a value or element away is remove. Local cannot be disconnected.

concept: A connected integration that cannot sync right now (GLOSSARY: Needs attention)
note: The state is shown as an action ("Verbindung prüfen", "Verbindung reparieren"), not as an error word (PRODUCT.md principle 5: no technical detail). The tasks stay usable. Avoid forms are about the connection state only: the plain "Fehler"/"error"/"failed" were dropped, they hit every genuine error message (32 values at seeding) which is a different concept.

concept: A task changes its source; it stays the same task (GLOSSARY: Move)
note: Never "copy": the original is deleted from the old source once the task exists in the new one. "kopieren"/"copy" alone were narrowed to "Aufgabe kopieren"/"copy task": the bare words hit clipboard actions ("ID kopieren", "Copy summary") and backup copies (14 values), a different concept.

concept: How a move names the source the task goes to (#841): the command palette row, the toast after the move and the children of the card and sheet menu
de: zum lokalen Speicher verschieben / zu {Quelle} verschieben
en: move to local storage / move to {source}
note: The user's wording of 2026-11-25 (#841); the user's `npm run terms:approve move-target` makes it decided. Keys source.moveTarget.* (palette), source.moveDone.* (toast, own sentence-initial form per source, never capitalised in code) and source.moveMenuName.* (children under "Verschieben zu …": "lokalem Speicher", "Notion"). Local reads "lokaler Speicher" only in a move; its name stays "Lokal" everywhere else (settings, "Speichern in", metadata). Moves between columns say "in „Spalte“" (4f513773), not this term. "„{title}“ bleibt in {source}." after a failed move keeps the plain name. English: the palette and the toast say "to local storage", but the menu children under "Move to …" stay the plain source names ("Local", "Notion"), as #841 AC 4 asks: the parent already says "Move to", so the child is the destination's name, not a phrase.

concept: Board column 1 (fixed order Offen, Jetzt, Wartet, Erledigt)
note: UI status labels are used in E2E assertions. board.columns.* in en.json holds "Open", "Now", "Waiting", "Done" (de label in de.json).

concept: Board column 2, the WIP-limited column (at most one task)
note: The key is board.columns.progress; the term is "Jetzt". "Aktuell"/"current" are not avoid forms: ordinary words (23 values such as "aktuell keine Datenquellen", "Replaces your current data"). Known collision: en "doing" hits the Notion status example "Today, Doing, Waiting, Done" (1 value), allow that key when deciding.

concept: Board column 3: waiting on something
note: en values containing "waiting": 9 at seeding.

concept: Board column 4: finished tasks
note: User answer (#485): a task's state is always erledigt / done; Fertig / Done only labels a button that closes a dialog; abschließen only for the day (Tag abschließen) or a setup. The allow list also exempts de errors.title.success "Fertig" (a success toast title, an open question); the 6 en task-state strings that said "finished" now say "done" (#491).

concept: The planned time for a task
note: User answer (#473): "Timebox". de "Timebox" 25 values, en "timebox" 24; no "Zeitbox"/"Zeitvorgabe" left. en "estimate" (14 values) is not an avoid form: estimation accuracy ("Estimated accurately", "your estimates") is a different concept from the planned box.

concept: A grouping label of a task (colour-coded)
note: de "Thema/Themen" 17 values, en "topic" 17; en "category" 8, de "Kategorie" 1. Avoid forms are matched as case-insensitive word prefixes, so they are narrowed: de "Tags" (the plural) instead of "Tag", because "Tag" also hits "Tage", "Tagen", "Tagesabschluss" and day-close's own "Tag abschließen"; the singular loanword "Tag" is not catchable. Known collisions today: "Label"/"label" also hit the placeholder name "{label}" (4 values each); en "tag" also hits "tagline" and "tagged" (no value today). Resolve the collisions with a per-key allow when the term is decided (not part of the calibration).

concept: The kind of work a task is (second grouping next to topic)
note: de "Aktivität" 15 values, en "activity" 12 (plus one "Activity" in de.json). en "action" is not an avoid form: it hits "More actions" and "update action" (2 values), other concepts.

concept: The free-text field of a task
note: User answer (#473): "Notiz" over "Notizen"/"Beschreibung", singular in both languages. The feedback message field "Beschreibung (optional)" (feedback.descriptionLabel) is a different concept and is allowed.

concept: Where deleted tasks sit until they are restored or purged
note: de "Papierkorb" 5 values, en "trash" 5.

concept: Delete data: a task (it goes to the trash first), a stored token, a draft
note: User answer (#473): data removal = Löschen. de "Löschen" 29 values, en "delete" 28. Different concepts: delete (data goes away), remove (a value or element is taken away, nothing deleted), disconnect (ends an integration). The GitHub token is stored data (Löschen), the feedback draft "Entwurf löschen" replaces "verwerfen".

concept: Take a value or an element away without deleting data (a timebox, a field value, a screenshot, a highlight)
note: de "Entfernen" 6 values (task.property.clear, task.contextMenu.removeTimebox, feedback.removeElement, feedback.screenshot.remove, feedback.annotate.drawHint, the checkbox sentence in settings.data.exportImport.failedSafety), en "remove" 5. Boundary to delete and disconnect: see those entries. "Löschen"/"delete" are not avoid forms here: they are the preferred forms of delete, and a term may not avoid another term's preferred form (checkTerms). The boundary is by concept, reviewed per string.

concept: Move finished tasks out of the board into the archive
note: de "Archiv*" 6 values, en 6. Known collision: de "Ablegen" also hits the drag-and-drop hint "Hier ablegen, um die Aufgabe abzuschließen" (1 value, allow that key).

concept: Bring a task back from the trash
note: de "Wiederherstellen" 16 values, en "restore" 15.

concept: Revert the last action right after it
note: de "Rückgängig" 3 values, en "Undo" 4. DESIGN.md: undo instead of confirm.

concept: Store the changes of a form
note: de "Speichern" 12 values vs "Sichern" 2; en "Save" 32. Narrowed: bare "Sichern"/"store" hit backups ("Jetzt sichern", "Stored on this device"), a different concept (3+2 values).

concept: Accept a suggestion (for example a suggested timebox)
note: common.apply and task.timeboxNudge.apply; save vs apply: save stores a form, apply takes a suggestion. Narrowed: bare "accept" hits "did not accept the change" (Keychain) and "not accepting more requests" (3 values).

concept: Leave a form or dialog without changes
note: de "Abbrechen" 3 values, en "Cancel" 7. "Zurück" (common.back) is navigation, not cancel.

concept: Close a dialog or sheet
note: de "Schließen" 6 values, en "Close" 10. Not for ending the day, see day-close.

concept: The end-of-day flow: look back at today and tidy the board
note: de "Tag abschließen" 4 values vs "Tagesabschluss" 1 (dayClose.markdown.heading, a generated heading); en "Close the day".

concept: The short look back at the previous day when a new day starts
note: Earlier form: "Kurzer Rückblick" / "Quick look back". recap.title and README/PRODUCT prose. The app bar segment while the recap is open is the shorter nav-recap ("Rückblick" / "Look back"). Narrowed: bare "Zusammenfassung"/"summary" hit the day summary export ("Copy summary", "Summary copied", 8 values) and "review" hits the feedback dialog ("Review and send"), other concepts.

concept: Exchange changes with an integration
note: de "Synchron*" 20 values and "Sync" 19; en "sync" 27. de "Abgleich" 1. Known collision: de "Aktualisieren" also hits the app updater ("App aktualisieren", 1 value); it cannot be told apart under word-prefix matching, allow that key.

concept: Time actually spent on a task
note: User answer (#485): the time spent on a task is 'Aufgewendete Zeit' / 'Time spent', not 'Zeit investiert' or 'Aufwand'. The running timer on a card keeps 'Bisher gearbeitet'.

concept: The place and the things a user can change
note: User answer (#485): Einstellungen / settings for the place and what can be changed; no Konfiguration / configuration.

concept: First guided setup of an integration
note: User answer (#485): the first guided setup of an integration; "Einrichtung" / "setup" is the noun.

concept: The product name in running text
note: "Kan-do" in German and English running text. PRODUCT.md "Name: Kan-do". The wordmark text `nav.brand` stays lowercase on purpose (DESIGN.md Navigation: the brand `kan-do` in the app bar pill) and is allowed. `productName`, the bundle identifier, the data folder and the updater and Keychain keys are not copy and keep their spelling.

concept: Form of address in German UI copy
note: docs/copy/voice.md "Address": du. The formal address is converted (#474). "Sie"/"Ihr"/"Ihnen" are matched case-sensitively (caseSensitive), so the pronoun "sie"/"ihre" (she/they/it) does not hit; the 4 sentence-initial pronouns "Sie bleibt…" are exempt via allow (keep the list to these keys: a new sentence-initial pronoun needs an allowed key).

concept: The last moment of a day the app saw: the tasks still in Offen, Jetzt or Wartet then are counted on the Statistik page (#537)
note: Not an exact time: the count is the last one the app saw that day, so a day on which the app was only open in the morning shows the morning count. Not to be confused with day-close (the dialog, "Tag abschließen").

concept: A task's required name, the first field of the add and detail sheets (#662)
note: The add-sheet placeholder asks to "benennen"/"name" the task and the empty-title error says "Gib der Aufgabe einen Titel." / "Give the task a title.": verb and noun differ on purpose (the field is a title, naming is the act).

concept: The statistics place: app bar segment, page title, browser tab title, open command (#680)
note: A place is named like the app bar names it ("Heute", "Statistik", "Papierkorb", "Einstellungen"): the singular, also as the page title and the tab title. de "Statistiken" was the page title and tab title before #680 while the app bar and the command said "Statistik". en was consistent ("Statistics" everywhere). "Statistik" inside running text ("zur Statistik hinzugefügt") is the same word.

concept: The third tab of Einstellungen: topics and activities, data and storage, updates and GitHub access (#691)
note: Earlier form: "Verwaltung" / "Manage". The tab and the sheet heading of the third settings tab. Named by the user in the #691 design round: user-data maintenance, not board behaviour, so Themen und Aktivitäten lives here too. The tab strip reads Board, Speicherorte, System. Not "Mehr" / "More" as a catch-all tab name; "Mehr" names the new-card flow's fourth cell (quick-add-more-values) and the registry test forbids one term's avoid form being another's preferred form.

concept: How many requests GitHub allows per hour; an optional read-only token raises it (update checks)
What a feedback report becomes on GitHub: a public issue in the app's repository
note: Earlier form: "Issue" / "issue". What a feedback report becomes on GitHub: the dialog says "Feedback" ("Als Feedback senden", "öffentliches Feedback", "Feedback-Text"). GitHub's own permission names stay as GitHub writes them ("Issues + Inhalte: schreiben"), and an issue number is written "#{number}".

concept: The user's own GitHub sign-in that the browser path of the feedback needs
note: Not the token: the token is the secret stored in the app (token entry); the account is the person's sign-in on github.com. German compound with the brand name takes a hyphen (DESIGN.md).

concept: The calendar day a task counts as done on: shown as a row of a done task's sheet, where a task marked done late is moved to the day the work was finished (kd#131)
note: Same wording as the Statistik table column (statistics.table.completedAt). Follows the decided task state erledigt / done (column-done). The Notion setup names Notion's own property and is not this row.

concept: Putting another task into Jetzt while one runs: the running task goes to Wartet, the other runs (#162)
note: Earlier form: "wechseln" / "switch". Toast "Aufgabe getauscht" / "Task swapped" and the drop announcement ("Beim Ablegen tauschen beide"). The code and the issue say swap. Other "wechseln" / "switch" in the UI (the data folder, the arrow-key deck) are different concepts. Not the Jetzt focus overlay.

concept: Erase everything the user created or connected and start again as on a first launch (kd#227)
note: The command, the section and the dialog say "App zurücksetzen" / "Reset app"; the effect is described with Löschen / delete (the decided data term). Proposed by the #227 build; the user decides.

concept: Hiding the cards of every other topic on the board so one stretch of work stays in view (#161)
note: Funnel "Thema", pill "Thema: <Name>, n ausgeblendet", ✕ "Thema beenden" (EN "Topic", "Topic: <name>, n hidden", "Clear topic"). Proposed by the #608 build (item 75, D2): "Fokus" stays the Jetzt focus overlay (settings.focus.*, #394), so the two features no longer share a word. The user decides. "Fokus" / "focus" are no avoid forms here: the word is the preferred form of the Jetzt focus features (settings.focus.*, the floating focus timer), and a word match cannot tell the features apart.

concept: The running count of days a task has been planned for (on the board); day 1 is the first day and stays silent (#121, #247). Days in "Alle Aufgaben" do not count (#356)
note: Changed in #356 from "Tag {n} auf dem Board" / "day {n} on the board": since a new day sends unfinished cards back, the count means the days a task was planned, not the days it lay on the board. The count is displayDay (stored days + 1), the same number on the card dots, the label and the sheet question ("seit {n} Tagen zur Erledigung eingeplant"). The label shows from day 2, so only the plural form exists.

concept: Who receives in-app feedback sent through the relay (#268): the people behind the app, named without a speaker
note: Earlier form: "Kan-Do-Team" / "Kan-Do team". The relay path files reports privately; the dialog names a recipient without "wir" / "we" (voice: the app has no speaker): "die Kan-do-Entwickler" / "the Kan-do developers". Chosen over "Entwickler" / "developer" to stay neutral; the project has one maintainer today.

concept: The point in the Offen list where the day's time is used up (#132, GLOSSARY: Capacity divider)
note: Earlier form: "Kapazität" / "Capacity". Label of the divider: "Deine Kapazität" / "Your capacity"; a compound or sentence may use the bare noun ("Kapazitätshinweis"). Not "Limit" (the WIP limit of Jetzt is a rule, this one only informs) and not "Warnung" (principle: calm, no alarm). Chosen in the design round of #132 (the user's own wording from decision D1).

concept: The length of the user's working day that the capacity divider assumes, set in Einstellungen (#306)
note: Label "Arbeitszeit pro Tag" / "Working hours per day"; the automatic choice is "Automatisch" / "Automatic" (learned from tracked work). Not "Kapazität" (that is the divider's own label) and not "Tageslänge".

concept: The place of the app bar where the day is planned (#354, epic #334): the column "Alle Aufgaben" beside the column of today's tasks
note: Named "Alle" / "All" (#435; first approved by the user on 2026-11-16, #367, then renamed "Planung" / "Planning" in #375, renamed back in #435, never made decided). The user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided. The route stays /all. "Backlog" is not the name of this place: it is an avoid form of column-open and not registered here, because an avoid form matches as a word prefix across every string.

concept: The column of "Alle" that lists the tasks kan-do holds that are not on today's board (#354)
note: User, 2026-11-20: the column's headline shows the short form "Alle" / "All" (design answer on #609); "Alle Aufgaben" / "All tasks" is the form for sentences and the region name (earlier forms: "Meine Aufgaben" / "My tasks", and before that "Nicht geplant" / "Not planned"). The user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided. Names the column only (headline, region name, sentences that say where a task goes); the state of a task there is the term not-planned-state. "Nicht geplant" is not an avoid form: it is that state's term.

concept: The state of a task kan-do holds that is not on today's board (#353): the fifth choice of the task sheet's status picker (#359) and the wording of sentences about it
note: Split from not-planned in #375, when the column became "Alle Aufgaben"; the wording itself was approved by the user on 2026-11-16 (#367). A state, like "Offen": "Status: Nicht geplant", "… ist nicht mehr für heute geplant.". Not "ungeplant" / "unplanned": that is ad-hoc work (task.isUnplanned, "Ungeplant"). Whether "chosen for today" is a marker separate from the status is #374.

concept: The headline of the Offen column on the place "Alle" (#375): there the only question is whether a task is for today
note: The user's wording of 2026-11-16 (#375). Only the headline (and the column's spoken name) on "Alle", key board.columns.openPlanning; on the place "Heute" the column is headed "Offen", and the status is "Offen" everywhere (column-open). The same word as the app bar's place "Heute" on purpose: both mean today's plan.

concept: The marker of a task that is part of today's plan, beside its status (#374, #793, #795): the task sheet's switch. A task is either planned for today or not, whatever its status (Offen, Wartet; Jetzt is always planned)
note: Proposed in the UX decision of #374 (D3, 2026-11-24); the user's `npm run terms:approve planned-for-today` makes it decided. The state of the move plan-for-today ("Für heute einplanen"), the way "Offen" is the state of a task. A marker, not a status: the four statuses are Offen, Jetzt, Wartet, Erledigt, and "Nicht geplant" (entry not-planned-state, decided: its concept and note still describe the fifth picker choice of #359 and need the user's update) is no longer a choice of the status picker. Label of the task sheet's switch in the row "Heute" (term planning-today).

concept: The move that puts a not-planned task on today's board, at the end of Offen (#354)
note: Approved by the user on 2026-11-16 (#367); the user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided. Name of the arrow button beside a card in "Alle Aufgaben". Proposed in the design of #334 (D4).

concept: The move that takes an Offen task off today's board; nothing is deleted (#354)
note: Earlier form: "Nicht heute" / "Not today". Card menu entry and name of the mirrored arrow. Approved by the user on 2026-11-16 (#367); the user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided. Proposed in the design of #334 (D4).

concept: The one green pill of the app bar on "Alle" that leads on to the board (#373; replaces the footer button "Tag starten" of #367)
note: The user's own German wording of 2026-11-16 (#373), English by the copy-writer skill; the user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided. It replaces "Tag starten" / "Start the day" (entry start-the-day, removed with the footer button), which had replaced the proposed "Weiter zu Heute". Unused since #454: the pill and key nav.continue are removed. "Board" is the user's word here, as in "Direkt zum Board" (straight-to-board).

concept: The fresh start of a new day (#387): the user's click that takes what was planned and not finished (Jetzt, Offen, Wartet) off the board, onto "Alle Aufgaben", and leads to "Alle", where the day is planned. The primary way out of the new-day recap (#356, epic #334) and the button of the notice on a board that was not started fresh
note: Approved by the user on 2026-11-16 (#367) as the recap's button; the user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided. Since #387 it is the fresh start itself and also the notice's button (the same action gets the same name; the working name "Frisch starten" of #387 is not used, decision D1 d there). The second way out is "Direkt zum Board". Since #428 the recap's button reads "Tag neu planen" (entry replan-the-day); the notice's button reads "Tag neu planen" too (#454), so this entry is unused.

concept: The secondary way out of the new-day recap: it skips planning, leads to the board and keeps it as it is (#356, #367, #387)
note: The user's own wording of 2026-11-16 (#367; the user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided); it replaces the proposed "Direkt zu Heute" / "Straight to Today" (entry straight-to-today). Also what Escape does on the recap. Since #428 the recap's secondary button reads "Überspringen und Board anzeigen" (entry skip-and-show-board); this entry stays for the history of the wording.

concept: The recap's primary button (#428): the fresh start of the new day, which archives yesterday's done tasks, takes the unfinished ones off the board and leads to "Alle"
note: The user's own German wording of 2026-11-17 (#428), English by the copy-writer skill; the user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided. It replaces "Tag planen" on the recap only (entry plan-the-day); since #454 the notice's button reads it as well (the same action gets the same name).

concept: The recap's primary button and the new-day notice's button (#724): the fresh start of the new day, which archives yesterday's done tasks, takes the unfinished ones off the board and leads to "Alle". It acknowledges the look back and starts planning a new day, not planning today over again
note: The user's own German wording of 2026-11-22 (#724), English by the copy-writer skill; the user's `npm run terms:approve plan-a-new-day` makes it decided. It replaces the decided entry replan-the-day, whose wording read as planning the current day over again; after approving this entry, remove replan-the-day by hand (approve does not drop it). Shown on the recap button, the notice's button and named in the notice's description.

concept: The recap's secondary button (#428): skips planning, leads to the board and keeps it as it is; archives nothing
note: The user's own German wording of 2026-11-17 (#428), English by the copy-writer skill; the user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided. It replaces "Direkt zum Board" (entry straight-to-board). Escape on the recap dismisses without a move, as before.

concept: The app bar's segment while the new-day recap is open (#428): it stands in for Alle and Heute and turns into them when the recap is left
note: nav.recap. The short form of the recap's headline (entry recap: "Tagesrückblick" / "Daily recap"); the user's mockup of 2026-11-17 (#428) shows "Rückblick". English "Look back" because the recap entry avoids "recap".

concept: The panel on top of "Alle Aufgaben" for one day: the tasks that were on the board yesterday (Jetzt, Offen and Wartet) and are still not planned (#356, #387, #469)
note: Earlier form: "Gestern auf dem Board" / "On the board yesterday". Proposed in the design of #469 (user answer D1: one panel, Wartet included). Replaces "Gestern geplant, noch offen" (planned-yesterday, approved 2026-11-16 in #367, never made decided) and "Zuletzt in Wartet" (was-waiting). The panel names the last board, not a date, so it reads the same when that board was longer ago.

concept: The last group of "Alle Aufgaben" while the panel "Zuletzt geplant und nicht erledigt" shows above it: every other task that is not planned (#356, #387)
note: Approved by the user on 2026-11-16 (#367); the user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided. Proposed in the design of #334. Shown only together with the panel above it.

concept: The panel on "Alle Aufgaben" for one day: the tasks the fresh start of today took out of Wartet and that are still not planned (#702)
note: No longer in the UI since #741 (one block, term from-yesterday). Second panel of #702, beside planned-yesterday. English "Waiting" is the column name Wartet.

concept: The block on top of "Alle Aufgaben" for one day: every task that was planned and not done when the board was last left (Jetzt, Offen and Wartet), named by the day they are from (#741, replaces planned-yesterday and waiting-yesterday of #702)
note: User decision on #741 (D2: one block, D3 2B: the title names the day). Forms: "Von gestern" the day before, "Von {weekday}" 2 to 6 days back ("Von Samstag"), "Vom {date}" beyond ("Vom 14. November"); English "From yesterday", "From {weekday}", "From {date}". A waiting task in it shows the badge "Wartet" (column-waiting).

concept: The button of a yesterday panel that plans all its tasks for today in one click (#702); the short form is used on a phone
note: Adapts the term plan-for-today ("Für heute einplanen"). Short form "Alle einplanen" / "Plan all" at 390px. The toast says "{n} Aufgaben sind für heute geplant." with "Rückgängig".

concept: The state of the marker beside the status: the task is part of today's plan (the switch of the task sheet's row "Heute", #795)
note: The state of plan-for-today, as in the epic #374's UI copy table. Beside the switch, while the task is in Jetzt, the hint reads "Jetzt gehört immer zu heute." / "Now is always part of today.". The row's label is planning-today.

concept: The mark of a task that was not planned but came up during the day (task.isUnplanned): the switch in the open Metadaten of the task sheet (#796; the card menu no longer sets it)
note: The line is from the epic #374's copy pass; Ad-hoc work is "Ungeplant" / "Unplanned" in the statistics (statistics.table.unplanned). Not "nicht geplant" (not-planned-state: a task off today).

concept: The question on the app's start or return after a night in which the Jetzt timer ran on while Kan-do was not in focus: take that time off the task again, or keep it (#356, the user's decision of 2026-11-16)
note: Proposed wording from the user's decision. Not "Entfernen": that term is for a value or element taken away; here a counted amount is subtracted from the total. Recorded time only changes when the user says so.

concept: The soft button of an empty "Alle Aufgaben" on the place "Alle": it opens the add form, and the new task is not planned (#367)
note: The user's own wording of 2026-11-16 (#367; the user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided), the same words as the add form's submit button (task.form.submit). The column header's icon button stays "Aufgabe hinzufügen" (board.addTask). The empty state beside it reads "Keine weiteren Aufgaben vorhanden.", also the user's wording.

concept: The answer to the sync question "Was trifft zu?" (#369) that leaves the board as it is and drops the fetched result; the footer button of that answer
note: The other footer button of the same dialog is "Änderung übernehmen" / "Apply the change" (the term `apply`). The dialog's title is "Kurz prüfen" / "Quick check": the design copy said "Bitte kurz prüfen", which the voice rule "No 'Bitte'" rules out.

concept: The small always-on-top window that shows the Jetzt task and its time over other apps while Kan-do is not in front (#383, ADR 020)
note: Earlier form: "Schwebendes Jetzt-Fenster" / "Floating Now window". The setting's label and the feature's name in prose; code, the route `/overlay` and ADR 020 keep "overlay". Not "Fokus": the board's dusk overlay (settings.focus, "Jetzt-Karte im Fokus") is a different feature. The window's buttons are "Pausieren" / "Fortsetzen" (EN Pause / Resume), "Als erledigt markieren" and "Kan-do öffnen" (the pill's aria-labels; the pill shows icons only).

concept: The first step of the Notion setup on the welcome page: what to have at hand before entering the token (#441)
note: Stepper label and hidden step heading; the intro pane itself has no visible heading.

concept: The Apple Reminders task source (#551, epic #481): the app on the Mac and the source name
note: Earlier form: "Erinnerungen" / "Reminders". The Apple Reminders task source (#551, epic #481): the app on the Mac and the source name `source.name.reminders`. Where the text names the macOS permission or its Settings path ("Systemeinstellungen › Datenschutz & Sicherheit › Erinnerungen") the system's own word stays, and "your reminders" as the items in the app are tasks of that source. In a German compound the two words are coupled with hyphens ("Apple-Erinnerungen-Einstellungen", `sourceCompound`, #685). Needs the user's `npm run terms:approve`.

concept: The ⋯ menu in the title row of the task sheet (#705): open in source, move to source, Delete
note: Proposed in the build of #705 (aria label of the sheet's ⋯ button, `task.detail.menuLabel`). The user's `npm run terms:approve` makes it decided.

concept: The page with the provider's identity and address (§ 5 DDG, § 18 MStV), on the maintainer's homepage (#745)
note: #745: link label in Einstellungen › System › Rechtliches, on the welcome page and in the feedback notice. English sentence case inside a sentence, "Legal notice" as a label.

concept: Kan-do's privacy notice (Art. 13 GDPR), its own page on the maintainer's homepage (#745)
note: #745: in a sentence "Datenschutzhinweise" / "privacy notice"; the short link label in a list of three is "Datenschutz" / "Privacy".

concept: Kan-do's terms of use, on the maintainer's homepage (#745)
note: #745: link label and the sentence at the Notion token step.

concept: The short hints on the board that show the next step of the first days, and the setting that turns them off and on (#725, #804)
note: #804: the settings row label. On a hint the link is the verb phrase "Hinweise ausschalten" / "Turn off hints"; the section that lists their texts is "Kurz erklärt" / "Quick guide".

concept: The setting that makes the whole interface larger or smaller in fixed steps (#845)
note: #845: the settings row label, in the sheet "Darstellung" / "Appearance". Not "Zoom": that word names the Window menu's item that enlarges the window (menu.zoom). The 100 % step is marked "(Standard)" / "(default)".
